title: Unchecked 1:1 phUSD minting with UNBALANCED addLiquidity causes suboptimal BPT returns when pool ratio diverges
description: The BalancerPooler always mints phUSD at a fixed 1:1 decimal-normalized ratio to the prime token and adds both as UNBALANCED liquidity to a Balancer pool. When the pool's actual ratio diverges from 1:1, the UNBALANCED addLiquidity results in fewer BPT than the fair value of the deposited tokens. The excess amount on the surplus side is effectively donated to existing LPs and extracted by arbitrageurs. Over time, as the pool ratio naturally drifts, each mint through this dispatcher systematically leaks value. The BPT goes to the BalancerPooler contract, so the protocol bears the loss directly.
impact: Protocol receives fewer BPT than fair value on every mint when pool ratio is not exactly 1:1. The cumulative value leak scales with the number of mints and the magnitude of pool ratio divergence.
rootCause: Line 83 always mints phUSD at 1:1 ratio (_normalizeToPhUSD). Lines 96-105 add UNBALANCED liquidity with equal amounts regardless of pool ratio. No mechanism adjusts the deposit ratio to match the pool.
recommendation: Consider using PROPORTIONAL addLiquidity (adjusting phUSD mint to match pool ratio), or add an oracle-based check on the exchange rate before minting. At minimum, enforce a configurable minimum BPT tolerance that is non-zero by default.
